_meta.task: recall_count contamination — does it change any output?
_meta.verdict: No. Do not build a fix. Document and move on.

contamination_extent.note: The 2152 figure over-counts. Most of those memories have other recalls too, so their recall_count is not solely an artifact. Only 477 have a single recall that lands on a sweep day.

measured_impact.method: clone the prod DB, zero recall_count for the 477 purely-contaminated rows, compare every consumer against the untouched clone

dream_demote_pass.note: The only difference anywhere. 35 of 5869 memories (0.6%) are not being demoted that should be. Demotion excludes a memory from the index — and the index is byte-identical between the two, so even this difference produces no observable change.

conclusion: The contamination is real and worth knowing about, but it is inert. A recall_count_since epoch column was scoped and would have been built for no measurable gain. session_analytics already detects and prints bulk-recall days, which is the right amount of effort to spend on this.
revisit_if: Active forgetting is ever enabled (MEMORY_ACTIVE_FORGET=1). That path soft-deletes on an activation score which reads recall_count and distinct_session_count, and unlike demotion it is destructive. Re-run this comparison before turning it on.
